is to place ambition in the pot of effort,simulate over a low heat of perseverance,and season it with judgment.Do you like this formula?I do like it in that it provides us with some new factors contributing to success.I appreciate Tad's taking judgment into consideration.Sometimes wise judgments at key moments are crucial.What's more,Tad's interpretation by using metaphors in Chinese,比喻,really helps the audience understand the formula.Good job!The following is a formula from our classmate Sam.According to the formula,Sam has taken passion, talent, and action into consideration.They are not simply added together.Instead,Sam multiplies the sum of passion and talent and action.It is fair to say that no matter how much passion or talent you have,if you don't take action,nothing can be achieved in the end.What a creative and rigorous formula you have made.Well done!Sam's formula reminds me of another formula put forward by Inamori Katsua,one of the four Japanese sages in management.He also has a formula which is regarded as the Bible in management by many people.This is his formula.What needs to be pointed out is that in this formula,all the factors are multiplied,which means not a single factor can afford to be zero.More importantly,the minimum of attitude can be as low as minus 100,which definitely means a negative attitude can be destructive.What a witty and educational formula it is.After sharing so many inspiring and witty formulas for success,I firmly believe that you have agreed on at least one of them,or you have come up with a unique one of your own.On the road to success,we may meet with obstacles and setbacks,but we will not get lost as long as we have the formula in hand and stick to it.This is the last period of this unit.It's necessary to assess your performance in this unit.Step one,check whether you have achieved the overall learning goals listed on page 17.Step two,reflect.Recall the activities you have
